nodes.description: All molecular subgroups arise from progenitor populations of the developing cerebellum and rhombic lip, and converge on dysregulated proliferation, but they do not share a single cell of origin. SHH tumors derive from external-granule-layer granule-neuron precursors; WNT tumors from lower-rhombic-lip / dorsal brainstem progenitors; and Group 3 and Group 4 (non-WNT/non-SHH) tumors from rhombic-lip-derived progenitors, with Group 4 in particular linked to the unipolar brush cell lineage. The subgroup-specific oncogenic pathways (WNT/beta-catenin, Sonic Hedgehog, MYC-driven programs) feed a common proliferative phenotype across these distinct progenitor lineages; while rare cases arise on a germline cancer-predisposition background (APC, SUFU, PTCH1, TP53), the neoplastic proliferation itself is driven by somatic clonal expansion in hindbrain progenitors. Cell Ontology includes CL:4023161 (unipolar brush cell), which represents the differentiated glutamatergic interneuron rather than the proliferative progenitor population, and has no rhombic-lip progenitor class, so the non-SHH progenitor lineages are bound to the generic neural progenitor cell class.

cell_types: cerebellar granule neuron precursor (SHH subgroup cell of origin)
rhombic lip-derived progenitor (WNT and non-WNT/non-SHH cell of origin)

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Stratification of Medulloblastoma: Clinical Outcomes and Therapeutic Interventions.
evidence.snippet: Medulloblastoma (MB) is the most common malignant pediatric posterior fossa tumor.
Classified as a World Health Organization (WHO) grade 4 embryonal tumor, medulloblastoma arises primarily in the posterior fossa, most often from the cerebellum.

nodes.description: Craniospinal irradiation (CSI) with a posterior-fossa/tumor-bed boost is standard for children >=3 years due to the risk of leptomeningeal dissemination. CSI is generally avoided or delayed in children <3 years to limit neurocognitive and neuroendocrine late effects, and dose-reduction trials evaluate lower-intensity CSI for low-risk WNT medulloblastoma.

evidence.snippet: Radiotherapy to the craniospinal axis with a boost to the posterior fossa has been standard practice, but improvement in radiotherapy techniques and quality control has enabled optimisation of the trade-off between tumour control and normal tissue late toxicities.

nodes.description: Multi-agent cytotoxic chemotherapy (commonly cisplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and lomustine) is standard adjuvant therapy after surgery and radiation. In infants and young children (<3 years), intensive chemotherapy regimens are used to delay or avoid craniospinal irradiation.

evidence.snippet: Combination chemotherapy is usually given adjuvantly, although it may be used to delay or avoid the use of radiotherapy in infants.

Despite advances in multimodal therapy, including surgical resection, craniospinal irradiation, and chemotherapy, medulloblastoma remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in children. Overall, 5-year survival ranges from 65% to 70%, with survivors frequently experiencing long-term neurocognitive and neuroendocrine complications.

nodes.description: Maximal safe resection is the first-line treatment across molecular subgroups to relieve fourth-ventricular CSF obstruction and achieve maximal cytoreduction. Extent of resection is prognostic; near-total or gross-total resection is achievable in most cases.

evidence.snippet: Advances in surgical techniques have allowed a greater attainment of the two primary surgical goals: restoring normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow and maximal tumour resection.
